subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Is it intentional for line-leading `System:` neutralization at the system-event queue, plus the existing trusted prompt narration and external-content envelopes, to replace the retired global bracket-tag de-fanging contract for all prompt-bound event sources?
rationale: The change is deliberate and the supplied tests cover the queue case, but accepting the reduced sanitizer scope is a security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical correctness judgment.

options.title: Confirm the narrowed boundary
options.body: Accept queue-level line-leading `System:` neutralization as the intended contract after the responsible owner confirms all prompt-bound system-event sources traverse that queue.

options.title: Retain broader sanitization
options.body: Restore a narrowly scoped shared sanitizer for any source that can reach model-bound text outside the verified queue boundary.

options.title: Pause the refactor
options.body: Keep the existing sanitizer until the desired prompt-injection boundary and upgrade behavior are explicitly documented and approved.

recommendation.title: Confirm the narrowed boundary
recommendation.body: Accept queue-level line-leading `System:` neutralization as the intended contract after the responsible owner confirms all prompt-bound system-event sources traverse that queue.
